subject: [PATCH v6 1/2] iommu/arm-smmu-v3: Add a cmdq_max_n_shift module parameter

2026-09-09.patch_summary: This patch adds a new module parameter called cmdq_max_n_shift to control the command queue depth in the ARM SMMUv3 driver. The parameter is used as a cap on the log2 of the number of entries in the queue, allowing users to limit the maximum queue size based on their system's memory constraints. Without this patch, systems with limited memory may fail to probe due to excessive queue sizes. The patch introduces a helper function arm_smmu_cmdq_max_n_shift() to calculate the queue depth and applies the parameter value to it. Additionally, the patch floors the requested queue size at one page worth of entries to prevent the SMMU from failing to probe.

reviews.author: Breno Leitao
reviews.summary: Expressed gratitude for fixing an issue he had previously encountered while investigating another SMMU problem. Did not provide any technical feedback or suggestions.
reviews.raw_body:
On Wed, Sep 09, 2026 at 10:52:27AM +0100, Kiryl Shutsemau (Meta) wrote:
> The command queue depth comes straight from the maximum the hardware
> advertises in IDR1, which reaches megabytes of coherent DMA per queue.
> A system with several SMMUv3 instances pays that per instance, and the
> Tegra241 CMDQV pays it again for every VCMDQ it preallocates.

Thanks. I've seen this issue while investigating another SMMU issue[1].
Thanks for fixing it.

Link: https://lore.kernel.org/all/20260911-smmu_fix_aws-v1-0-75870bf9655b@debian.org/ [1]

> Queue depth only bounds how many commands may be in flight before a sync.
> A machine driving a handful of devices, or one with a tight memory budget,
> has no use for the maximum, and no way to say so.
> 
> Add cmdq_max_n_shift, a cap on the depth given as the log2 of the entry
> count, the form the hardware itself takes in the LOG2SIZE field of
> CMDQ_BASE. Decide the depth in arm_smmu_cmdq_max_n_shift(), which caps the
> IDR1 value for natural alignment and then applies the parameter, so the
> queue is allocated at the requested size. The Tegra241 CMDQV sizes its
> VCMDQs from IDR1 itself, so route that through the same helper.
> 
> Floor the request at one page worth of entries. Without the floor, a small
> request trips the CMDQ_BATCH_ENTRIES check in arm_smmu_device_hw_probe()
> and the SMMU fails to probe. The floor also costs nothing: coherent DMA is
> page granular, so a shallower queue occupies the same memory as one that
> fills the page.
> 
> Assisted-by: LLM
> Signed-off-by: Kiryl Shutsemau (Meta) <kas@kernel.org>

Reviewed-by: Breno Leitao <leitao@debian.org>

2026-09-15.patch_summary: This patch introduces a new module parameter, cmdq_max_n_shift, which allows users to cap the command queue depth for SMMUv3 devices. The queue depth is currently set to the maximum value advertised by the hardware, but this can be problematic for systems with limited memory or tight budgets. The new parameter enables users to specify a custom log2 depth ceiling, ensuring that the queue never shrinks below one page.
